name: Puerto de Almería & Parque de las Almadrabillas
story: Almería's harbour was the arrival point for tens of thousands of refugees from Málaga in February 1937, and the target of the German naval bombardment of 31 May 1937. After the war, many Andalusian Republican exiles who had fled to France were captured by the Germans in 1940 and sent to Mauthausen; of about 1,500 who passed through the camp only about 500 survived. The memorial in the Parque de las Almadrabillas by the port remembers them.
see: The harbour front and the memorial to the Mauthausen deportees in the Almadrabillas park.
plan: 10 minutes' walk from the shelters; open access.

boxes.text: Numbers of Andalusian deportees to Mauthausen vary between sources.
